title: Policy gateway: schema hardening and runtime mapping for region/tier fallback
creator: Samuel Park
description:
Summary: Refactor the policy gateway to separate declarative rule schema validation from runtime routing decision mapping. The goal is to harden the DSL/config schema (region selectors, tier routing weights, and fallback model variant declarations) while keeping runtime path minimal-latency and safe for rolling migration.

Background: Current policy parsing mixes validation, compatibility migration, and runtime interpretation. This has caused subtle production issues when we introduced region-based asymmetric rules and tiered fallbacks (seen in incident notes on Confluence). We need a clearer contract: declarative schema + typed AST + deterministic runtime matcher.

Goals:
- Implement a stricter schema with backward-compatible migration layers that reject malformed or ambiguous rules during CI and during config apply (but can optionally allow a permissive compatibility flag for legacy customers).
- Generate a compact, precompiled runtime map from validated configs: a small, efficient matcher used in hot paths that minimizes allocations and avoids regex parsing on request path.
- Support explicit region selection, tier routing (gold/silver/beta), and a deterministic fallback ordering across model variants and regions.
- Provide clear error telemetry and actionable operator messages to fix bad rules.

Design decisions so far:
- Use a JSON Schema v2020 draft for initial surface validation plus a typed AST layer (TypeScript schema -> typed AST generator) for richer semantic checks (e.g., validating that region sets are disjoint when explicit disjointness required). JSON Schema will catch shape; typed AST will catch cross-field constraints.
- Add a staged migration: incoming configs are validated against both the new schema and legacy parser during a migration window. A warning-only mode will be used for 4 weeks before enforcement.
- Runtime artifacts: compile validated AST to a compact table format: region bitmap (uint64 bitmask) + tier priority lists + variant fallback arrays. This keeps runtime lookups to O(1)-ish bit operations and small array scans rather than expensive tree traversal.
- Fallback strategy: explicit variant order in rule -> regional fallback -> tier fallback -> global default model. The policy engine will surface the chosen fallback reasoning for observability.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict vs permissive validation: strict validation reduces runtime surprises but may break customers with edge-case rules. We will mitigate with a 4-week warning window and a permissive compatibility flag.
- Full AST at runtime vs compiled table: full AST gives flexibility but increases allocations and CPU on hot path; compiled table trades flexibility for lower runtime cost. We chose compilation for p99 latency reasons.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI stage rejects configs that violate new schema unless compatibility flag set.
- New precompile step produces identical routing decisions as legacy parser for canonical test vectors.
- End-to-end performance: no more than 5% increase in p50 and under 10% in p99 for routing decision time compared to baseline (measured in staging).
- Telemetry: invalid-rule counts and top-5 offending rules surfaced in console; per-apply diagnostics available to operators.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Policy+Gateway+Schema+Hardening+Design
- Initial PR with typed AST generator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/432
- Benchmarks: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/abc123/policy-runtime-bench (staging runs)
- Migration runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-migration-runbook

Next steps / tasks:
- (ENG) Implement JSON Schema + typed AST generator and add to policy-engine repo (owner: Aisha).
- (ENG) Create precompile output format + deserializer used by runtime; add unit tests for all canonical vectors (owner: Miguel Torres).
- (SRE/Product) Draft warning communication to customers in migration window (owner: Lina Patel).
- (DX) Console: add telemetry panels for invalid rule counts and a per-config diagnostics viewer (owner: Priya Anand).

Risks:
- Edge-case rules used by large-enterprise customers may require one-off compatibility shims. We'll gate enforcement by account and provide a support path.
- Performance regressions on very-high-QPS routes; we will measure and, if needed, implement LRU caches for compiled tables per-tenant.

Estimated effort: 6-8 dev-weeks across two engineers + 1 week for console and runbook.
comments: [2025-02-14] Kickoff sync: Align on migration window (4 weeks) and permissive flag approach. Action: Aisha to prototype schema and AST generator by next week.
[2025-02-21] Prototype complete: typed AST generator implemented; initial test vectors added. Early benchmark shows 12% improvement in routing lookup vs legacy interpreter. See PR #432.
[2025-02-28] Review feedback from PM (Jonas Müller): prefer explicit union type for "tier" field to avoid free-form labels. Also requested clearer error messages for ambiguous region sets.
[2025-03-03] Security review kickoff: discussed potential injection vectors in DSL (we already sanitize interpolations). Security recommends adding a policy lint for suspicious negative lookups.
